title: SCOPE — 13 of Uzbekistan's 31 gas rows are Kazakhstan's rows, deliberately NOT researched here, and they DEPEND on the Kazakhstan batch being applied first
summary: Uzbekistan is a transit country, so a cross-border trunk is ONE sheet row that both the Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan --country scopes select. Thirteen rows (P0739, P0740, P1124, P2289, P2291, P2292, P2299, P2300, P3956, P5695, P5770, P5771, P5810) already carry staged records from the Kazakhstan pass; re-researching them here would stage contradictory records on the same cells and the last workbook pasted would win silently. Baird set this batch's research scope to the 18 DOMESTIC rows (31 rows / 283 ref units -> 18 rows / 152 units), enforced by build_ref_worklist.py --exclude-pids off batches/uzbekistan-gas/carried_from_kazakhstan.txt, which is derived from Kazakhstan's own staged_resolutions.json and never hand-typed. VERIFIED IN THIS PACKET: all 152 ref-class units and every staged action belong to the 18 domestic rows; zero of the 13 appear anywhere in staged_actions.json. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE RESEARCHER: until the Kazakhstan batch is applied, NEITHER batch researches those 13 rows. They are not cleared, not audited, and not covered by anything in this packet -- apply Kazakhstan first, then treat them as Kazakhstan's rows. THE EXCLUSION STOPS AT THE RESEARCH LEGS: the recon leg deliberately keeps all 31 GEM rows, because dropping the trunks would make their reference counterparts re-bucket as DISCOVERY_CANDIDATE and manufacture phantom additions for pipe GEM already tracks. Note also that Leg-3's worklist.json still lists all 27 flagged rows including the 13 -- auto-discovery is by country+commodity and cannot subtract another country's packet, so any future fan-out must be re-scoped to the 14 domestic flagged rows by hand.

title: GulfPub: the >10% status-conflict gate is crossed on paper (18.75%) and EMPTY in fact -- all 9 conflicts are one row pair, and the cause is a GEM data defect, not a source disagreement
summary: 9 of 48 overlaps carry a status conflict = 18.75%, over the >10% escalation gate. Every one of the 9 is the single pair P6963/P6964 (Yangiyer-Ahangaran), all reading construction -> operating. EXCLUDING that pair the rate is 0 of 33 = 0.00%. The 9 conflicts come from 3 GulfPub features located in Karakalpakstan/Khorezm (lon 56-60, lat 41-45) while P6963/P6964 run Yangiyer (Sirdaryo) -> Ahangaran (Tashkent), roughly 800 km away; they matched on s_diameter 1.0 plus s_length 0.68-0.89 against a g_score of only 0.06-0.15. CAUSAL CHAIN: P6964's LengthEstimateKm of 111.29 km is itself an artifact of its own off-corridor drawn route (redundancy cluster E), so it coincidentally length-matches 106-180 km northwestern features. Fix cluster E and the gate dissolves -- do NOT work these 9 as source disagreements. 15 of the 48 overlaps land on this one pair. Cluster E now has FOUR independent corroborations: the attribute sweep, the off-corridor geometry measurement, route_integrity's endpoint_country flag (the drawn route exits into Kyrgyzstan), and this GulfPub mis-attribution.

title: OSM: 124 additions crosses the >30 gate on VOLUME alone -- it is a scope/granularity mismatch, not 124 discoveries
summary: The OSM extract returned 124 gas records against 31 GEM rows, 0 of which matched at the 0.45 composite gate (max composite 0.4411), so all 124 bucket as unmatched additions -- over the >30 gate. Read them as scope, not discovery: 69 of the 124 features are sub-1 km stubs, and 52.6% of total reference mileage lies within 2 km of an existing GEM route vertex, i.e. the majority of the mileage is distribution-scale detail hanging off pipe GEM already tracks. The run also fires MATCH_QUALITY on the name axis (only 2 of 124 features are named, and both names are RUSSIAN -- Uzbekistan is the third Cyrillic scope, so normalize.translit_cyrillic is load-bearing here). That MATCH_QUALITY is a TRUE report about a genuinely nameless extract, not a tuning signal: 29 of 31 GEM rows are routed and 16 are RouteAccuracy 'high', so the dead-both-axes condition that the warning is designed to catch does not hold. See the geoarea escalation for why no override was added.

title: OUR OWN TUNING QUESTION, settled empirically and REFUSED: gas_uz ships with NO geoarea_weight override, because the override manufactures corroboration
summary: The obvious response to a 0-overlap OSM run is to enable the geoarea axis for this dataset. We ran that A/B into a scratch staging dir (manifest backed up and md5-verified restored afterwards, so no committed run moved). At geoarea_weight 0.30 the run produces 4 overlaps, 83.1% of records geoarea-scored, and MATCH_QUALITY goes silent -- and THREE OF THE FOUR ARE MANUFACTURED: a 1.625 km stub and a 0.036 km (36 metre) stub each 'corroborate' the same ~350 km GEM row at route IoU 0.029 and 0.027, clearing the gate on s_geoarea = 1.0 alone. That happens because 69 of the 124 features are sub-1 km and every one of them is trivially in the right province. Contrast gas_iq / gas_pk, where stub fragments sit ON the GEM corridor and are therefore TRUE matches to be labelled PARTIAL (reconcile.coverage()'s documented design). Geoarea is additionally untestable on 9 of the 18 domestic rows (P2290, P2698, P3983, P3984, P6933-P6935, P6965, P6966 -- the Gazli-Kagan and Mubarek clusters), so it would not even help where the sweep needs help. DECISION: no override. Do not revisit this without re-running that A/B; the reasoning is recorded in sources/osm/manifest.yml under the gas_uz block.

title: Route geometry: P4071's Tajikistan crossing is a schematic ARTIFACT, but P6936/P6937 put vertices 14-36 km inside AFGHANISTAN -- redraw both, and do NOT add Afghanistan to CountriesOrAreas
summary: route_integrity flagged 3 rows on country grounds. Measured against actual borders: (1) P4071 -- both vertices are in Uzbekistan but the LINE crosses Tajik territory, because the route is a 2-vertex straight chord from Ahangaran toward Pungan and the direct chord clips the Tajik salient on the Fergana Valley approach. That is a digitizing artifact of a 2-vertex schematic, NOT a CountriesOrAreas defect; no country-column change is warranted, and the real fix is a redraw. (It compounds redundancy cluster B, which already stages P4071/P4072's StartState 'Fergana' -> Namangan.) (2) P6936 (Kelif-Mubarek) has an Afghan vertex 36.09 km from Uzbekistan and 19.65 km from Turkmenistan. (3) P6937 (Kelif-Dushanbe) has Afghan vertices 35.83 km, 16.34 km, 0.77 km and 14.54 km inside Afghanistan plus a Tajik vertex 49.40 km in. Only the 0.77 km value is Amu Darya border slop; 14-36 km is not, so these two drawn routes genuinely place pipe in Balkh/Jowzjan. Soviet trunk planning makes an Afghan transit unlikely, so the prior is a coarse schematic cutting a bend of the Amu Darya -- but that prior was NOT confirmable in this session (see the blocked-research escalation), so BOTH readings stay open. Do not add Afghanistan to either row's country list on this evidence, and do not treat the drawn geometry as authoritative for length.

title: Half of Uzbekistan's existing filled reference cells are dead links -- 39 of 78, and the survivors are what this packet re-verified
summary: Link rot was measured twice on this scope. Of the 78 ref cells that were already filled on the sheet, 39 carry a dead or missing link -- exactly half. Separately, 118 URLs harvested from gem.wiki resolved to 80 live / 14 true 404-410 / 14 BLOCKED / 8 timeout-DNS-5xx. The 14 blocked and 8 network failures are NOT deletions and must not be dropped from any cell (standing rule: only a confirmed 404/410 may remove a ref; a blocked origin gets its Wayback snapshot ADDED alongside, never swapped in). Confirmed 404s worth naming: utg.uz/ru/about/history/. Also note adilet.zan.kz-style TLS quirks do not apply here, but the general rule does: a full-text keyword miss is not evidence a ref fails when the supporting detail lives in a figure or map.

title: WAYBACK CONTENT IS UNREADABLE FROM THIS SESSION BY BOTH AVAILABLE PATHS -- 11 units rest on a capture whose bytes we did not read, 5 of them on that capture ALONE
summary: Measured 2026-08-26, twice, at the start and the end of the pass: archive.org's CDX/availability API answers in ~0.5s, while web.archive.org CONTENT serving is unreachable from this machine (curl, 3 attempts, 45s timeout each, http=000) AND is refused to the harness fetcher outright. So capture EXISTENCE is provable here and capture CONTENT is not, by any path available in this session. That is a network/tooling condition on our side and is NOT evidence about any source -- per the standing access-failure rule, none of these count as deletions and no live ref was dropped for one. Exact exposure: 11 staged units cite a Wayback capture (5 distinct captures: 20220517023637, 20240703031409, 20250905224526, 20260211121103, 20260314231446). For 6 of them a live non-Wayback leg carries the value independently, so the Wayback URL is belt-and-braces. For 5 -- P3983 Status, P3984 Length, P6964 Status/Fuel/PipelineType, all tier medium -- the capture is the ONLY leg, so re-fetch and confirm the value is on the page before pasting those five, or leave the cell. A SELF-CORRECTION belongs in this item: P6933 Owner [ref] was staged asserting a clean read of capture 20260314231446 (of the confirmed-404 utg.uz/ru/about/history/) with no caveat, at tier high with 'Independent? yes' -- while this very escalation recorded that same capture as unread. Corrected: the Wayback verification is now flagged existence-confirmed-by-API / content-not-read, and the unit's support is stated to rest on its live lex.uz/docs/537622 leg alone. It keeps tier high because lex.uz is a primary/regulatory source and the rubric allows high on a single primary source, but it no longer claims corroboration it does not have. Every other Wayback leg in the batch was already flagged existence-only; that one was the exception, and it is the reason to distrust a 'read it' claim that arrives without a flag.

title: OPERATOR RESOLVED for 8 of 9 rows despite the session's WebSearch budget being exhausted; TWO questions remain genuinely open (P2698's operator, P6936's start year)
summary: The Leg-3 fan-out was authorized and dispatched, then hit a hard blocker: this session's WebSearch quota was fully consumed (200/200) and every search-engine WebFetch fallback returns a CAPTCHA wall or 403. Confirmed from the main loop, not taken on a subagent's word. RESOLVED ANYWAY, by direct fetches to known origins: Uztransgaz's own organizational-structure page names its regional trunk-pipeline directorates (MGQB) with province/district seats and the stated function of operating trunk gas pipelines; its history page records Presidential Decree 4388 of 9 July 2019 splitting Uztransgaz out of Uzbekneftegaz into transmission (Uztransgaz) and distribution (Hududgaztaminot) and calls it sole operator of the national trunk network; and gazeta.uz independently reports a trunk line 'belonging to the Gazli Directorate of Main Gas Pipelines'. All URLs passed url_verifier. That staged 4 upgrades (P2290, P6934, P6936, P6937 -- each was UNRESOLVED/low, now REFS_ADDED/medium), 4 new medium fills where BOTH endpoints are named directorate seats (P3983, P3984 Gazli-Kagan via Gazli MGQB + Kogon MGQB; P6965, P6966 Mubarek-Kagan via Muborak MGQB + Kogon MGQB), and 2 low/UNRESOLVED fills where only ONE endpoint is (P4073 Gazli-Nukus -- Nukus is the seat of no listed branch; P5870 Gazli-Sarymay -- Sarymay CS could not be located against any directorate). MEDIUM, NOT HIGH, IS DELIBERATE: no document names any of these pipelines together with its operator, so the per-line attribution is inference from a sourced national sole-operator regime plus endpoints that are directorate seats. STILL OPEN, and these are the whole remaining research surface: (1) P2698 Shurtan-Sherabad's operator -- Uztransgaz publishes NO directorate for Surxondaryo, Sherobod, Termiz, Denov or Qarshi, and independently this row's Owner1 is 'Uzbekneftegaz', not Uztransgaz, so two signals agree it is the odd row out. Do NOT default it to Uztransgaz. (2) P6936 Kelif-Mubarek's StartYear1 -- carried as operating with no start year at all; also unresolved is whether the Kelif corridor's Afghan geometry is a mis-drawn schematic or real transit, and whether the separate Soviet-era Sheberghan/Khoja Gogerdak -> Mubarek export line out of Afghanistan is the origin of that geometry. Re-run those two in a fresh session. Nothing was manufactured to close them: they are staged UNRESOLVED, the honest class. METHOD NOTE FOR FUTURE PASSES: url_verifier's `verify_url` defaults to fuzzy=True, so it CANNOT be used to prove a token is ABSENT from a page -- a fuzzy check wrongly reported 'Qarshi' and 'Surxondaryo' present on the org-structure page, where the raw HTML has Qarshi nowhere and Surxondaryo only inside a province <select> in the site chrome. Use a raw fetch plus grep for absence claims.

title: RESOLVED 2026-08-27 by Baird's ruling: gem.wiki is never a source, WIKIPEDIA IS CITABLE -- source_roster.md's ban is withdrawn, no verifier change needed
summary: The policy question raised by this packet has been answered. Wikipedia is an acceptable [ref]; the only wiki that stays forbidden is GEM's own (standing rule 1 is about self-citation, not encyclopedias). docs/reference/source_roster.md's "never cite directly" line is withdrawn and replaced by a citable-with-conditions section: Wikipedia tiers as ONE secondary source (medium alone, green only when paired with an independent second source); two language editions of the same article are ONE source, not two, because the interwiki text is usually a translation; the underlying footnote is still preferred where the article carries one; and an article whose own footnote is GEM cannot corroborate anything, since a GEM figure copied into Wikipedia and cited back is still GEM. No code change was required -- wikipedia.org was never in url_verifier.BLOCKLIST_HOSTS -- so the retroactive exposure (Ukraine 141, Iran 72, Libya 47, Kazakhstan 40, Saudi gas 38, Egypt 26, India 19, Pakistan 16 mentions, plus 36 live [ref] cells on the GGIT gas tab) is legitimate rather than a cleanup backlog. NO CLEANUP SHEET WRITE IS OWED. Consequence for this packet: the one Wikipedia citation the harvest declined on principle (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Asia-China_gas_pipeline, on P2030) is now eligible and was re-tested.

title: OUR OWN COVERAGE GAP, measured after delivery: the wiki harvest pulled 127 unique citations and 88 WERE NEVER OPENED -- the ref legs satisfied cells instead of exhausting the pool
summary: Of 127 unique citation URLs harvested off the 18 gem.wiki pages, only 21 distinct URLs were used (they carry the source on 55 of the 90 paste-ready cells, across 14 of 18 rows), 12 were correctly declined by rule (11 gem.wiki/GEM self-references under standing rule 1; 1 Wikipedia, which the 2026-08-27 ruling has since made eligible), 6 were opened and rejected on the merits -- and 88 were never fetched at all. CAUSE, and it is a design flaw not an oversight: the ref legs were written to satisfy each owed unit (ProjectID x ref column), so a subagent stopped at the first sufficient source and never came back for the remaining citations on that page. Nothing in the leg's contract required the harvested pool to be exhausted, and nothing reported the shortfall -- the packet's UNRESOLVED count therefore reads as "no source exists" when for some cells it means "a candidate was never opened". SCOPE: 83 of the 88 sit on rows that still report UNRESOLVED, but 72 of those are on the two PARENT-TRUNK pages -- 49 on Central Asia-China (P2030) and 23 on Bukhara-Tashkent-Bishkek-Almaty (P6933/P6934/P6935) -- whose citations describe the trunk line, not the Uzbek string the row is about, which is exactly the documented wiki-ref trap and makes declining them correct. Real untested yield is therefore ~11 URLs on P2290, P2698, P3983, P3984, P4071, P4072, P6937, P6966, against cells owed for Diameter, Capacity, Owner, Length, Start and Location. RULE GOING FORWARD: the harvested pool is a WORKLIST, not a lookup table -- a ref leg must report how many harvested citations it opened, and an unopened citation sitting on a row with an owed cell is an open item, never a silent pass. CLOSED HALF-WAY, 2026-08-27: all 90 full URLs from the unopened set were run through url_verifier.verify_url as a reachability screen -- 55 LIVE / 35 FAILED. Only 12 of the failures are confirmed 404/410, i.e. genuinely removed; the other 23 are access failures that the standing rule explicitly does NOT treat as deletions (5x401, 5x403, 3x412, 4 ConnectTimeout, 2 ReadTimeout, 2 access-block-served-as-200, 1x429, 1x521). So the untested pool is now a MEASURED 55-URL reading list rather than an unknown, and 16 of the 55 sit on rows outside the two parent-trunk pages.

title: A REACHABILITY PASS IS NOT A READ -- utg.uz serves soft 404s, so 'live' in the screen above is a weaker claim than it looks
summary: Discovered 2026-08-27 while reading the highest-value URL out of the 55-live list. https://utg.uz/ru/press-service/novosti/korporativnye-novosti/stroitelstvo-novogo-magistralnogo-gazoprovoda-yangier-akhangaran-prodolzhaetsya/ returns HTTP 200 with 139,482 bytes -- and a deliberately nonsense slug in the same section returns HTTP 200 with 139,384 bytes, i.e. within 100 bytes of it, with no article body in either. The article is a SOFT 404: the news section serves the site template for any slug. The screen called it live because the screen only asked whether the host answered. Note the asymmetry within one site: /ru/invest/ DOES return a real 404 for a bogus slug, so the behaviour is section-specific and cannot be inferred from the host. CONSEQUENCE for this packet: nothing has to be un-staged -- these 88 were harvested CANDIDATES, never filled sheet cells, so no ref is being deleted -- but the one press release that might have settled the batch's only real recon conflict (P6963/P6964, GulfPub says operating, GEM says under construction) is unreadable at the origin, and this session cannot check its Wayback capture (web.archive.org timed out again on 2026-08-27, consistent with escalation 7). P6963/P6964's status therefore stays OPEN, and the WebSearch budget is still exhausted, so it needs a fresh session. RULE: a URL that passes a reachability screen is a candidate to READ, never a citable ref -- and where a soft 404 is suspected, prove it by fetching a nonsense sibling slug and comparing the bodies.

title: READ from the untested pool, 2026-08-27: Uztransgaz's own investor page is real and dated, but it is NOT a ref for any pipeline cell
summary: https://www.utg.uz/ru/invest/aktsii-i-dividendy/ is a genuine page (a bogus sibling slug 404s properly) carrying Uztransgaz's share-capital structure as at 01.04.2024: Ministry of Economy and Finance of Uzbekistan 329,807,303 shares / 51.7%, JSC Uzbekneftegaz 292,785,159 / 46.78%, the Presidential Administration's Center for Economic Research and Reforms 509 / 0.000081%, 11 legal entities 18,277 / 0.02%, 16,659 individuals 3,165,824 / 0.5%, total 625,777,072. It was harvested against ten rows (P2290, P3983, P3984, P6933-P6937, P6965, P6966). It is DECLINED for all of them, on the unit rule rather than on quality: it describes who owns the COMPANY, and the owed cells ask who owns or operates a PIPELINE, which the page never names. It does corroborate the sourcing chain behind this batch's medium-tier operator attributions (a state-controlled sole operator), and it is the right citation if a future pass needs Uztransgaz's own corporate ownership -- so it is recorded as opened and declined on the merits, not skipped.
